faq.hero_subtitle: Everything remote owners and foreign investors need to know about property management in Târgu Mureș and Transylvania.
faq.q1_q: What does a property manager do in Romania?
faq.q1_a: A property manager in Romania handles the full lifecycle of your rental: marketing the property, screening tenants, drafting lease contracts, collecting rent, coordinating maintenance and repairs, paying utility bills, and ensuring compliance with local laws. At Velox Living we also conduct regular inspections and send you photo reports so you always know the condition of your property. Think of us as your trusted representative on the ground — available to act even when you are thousands of kilometres away.
faq.q2_q: How much does property management cost in Transylvania?
faq.q2_a: Property management fees in Transylvania typically range from 8% to 15% of the monthly rent, depending on the scope of services included. At Velox Living, our full-service packages cover everything from tenant placement to bill payments and maintenance coordination — with no hidden charges. We believe transparent, predictable pricing is essential for remote owners who need to plan their rental income accurately.
faq.q3_q: What languages does Velox Living operate in?
faq.q3_a: Velox Living is fully operational in English, Romanian, Hungarian, and Spanish. This is especially important in Târgu Mureș, where both Romanian and Hungarian are widely spoken, and for our international clients based in Western Europe or Latin America. You can communicate with us in whichever language is most comfortable — from the initial consultation right through to monthly owner reports.
faq.q4_q: How quickly can Velox Living respond to maintenance emergencies?
faq.q4_a: For critical emergencies — burst pipes, heating failures, power outages — we respond as quickly as possible, including outside business hours. For routine maintenance, we coordinate a contractor visit within 24–48 hours. Our network of trusted local tradespeople — plumbers, electricians, locksmiths — means we never waste time searching for help when something needs fixing quickly.
faq.q5_q: Can a foreigner own and rent out property in Romania?
faq.q5_a: Yes — EU citizens have had the same property ownership rights as Romanian nationals since 2007, and non-EU nationals can own apartments and commercial spaces without restriction. Renting out your property is perfectly legal: you register the rental contract with the local tax authority (ANAF), declare your rental income, and pay a flat income tax. Velox Living handles all the local administrative steps on your behalf so you never need to visit a government office in person.
faq.q6_q: What are the legal requirements for renting an apartment in Târgu Mureș?
faq.q6_a: In Târgu Mureș, as across Romania, a legally valid rental requires a written lease contract signed by both parties, registration of that contract with ANAF within 30 days, and the declaration of rental income for tax purposes. The property must also hold a valid energy performance certificate (certificat energetic) before it can be advertised. Our team prepares all contracts in compliance with Romanian civil law and handles ANAF registration for you.
faq.q7_q: Do I need to be present in Romania to sign contracts with tenants?
faq.q7_a: No — as a Velox Living client, you do not need to travel to Romania to sign tenant contracts. We sign a property management contract together, through which Velox Living officially represents you as the owner — and it is this contract that allows us to conclude the lease agreement with the tenant on your behalf. All documents are signed digitally, so geography is never an obstacle to managing your investment.
faq.q8_q: How do I find reliable tenants in Transylvania?
faq.q8_a: Finding reliable tenants starts with professional marketing — quality photos, accurate listings on major Romanian portals, and clear pricing — combined with thorough screening. At Velox Living we verify employment, run reference checks, and review financial standing before recommending any applicant. Our local market knowledge in Târgu Mureș means we understand exactly which tenant profiles suit which neighbourhoods and property types.
faq.q9_q: What happens if a tenant doesn't pay rent in Romania?
faq.q9_a: Romanian law provides landlords with a clear process: if a tenant misses rent payments, the landlord can issue a formal notice and, if unresolved, initiate eviction proceedings through the courts. In practice, we act before disputes escalate — proactive communication, clear lease terms, and security deposit clauses protect our owners. Velox Living monitors payments every month and contacts tenants immediately if a deadline is missed, so problems are resolved early.
faq.q10_q: How are utility bills handled for rental properties in Romania?
faq.q10_a: In Romania, utility contracts (electricity, gas, water, building association fees) can be held in either the landlord's or tenant's name — the arrangement is specified in the lease. For owners living abroad, Velox Living can hold the utility accounts and pay bills on your behalf, recovering costs from the tenant each month. This keeps accounts organised, avoids late-payment penalties, and ensures nothing slips through the cracks while you're overseas.
faq.q11_q: What happens during a property inspection?
faq.q11_a: Velox Living conducts inspections at move-in, periodically during the tenancy, and at move-out. Each inspection includes a written condition report with photographs, shared with you digitally. This documentation protects you legally, helps track the property's condition over time, and provides an objective basis for assessing any deposit deductions at the end of a tenancy.
faq.q12_q: How do I get started if I live abroad and own property in Târgu Mureș?
faq.q12_a: Getting started is simple and requires no in-person visit. Begin by scheduling a free consultation via our website or WhatsApp — we'll discuss your property, your goals, and the best management package for your situation. We then send you a management agreement to sign digitally, and from that point we handle everything: inspections, listings, tenant placement, and ongoing management. Many of our clients have handed us the keys remotely and never looked back.
faq.cta_text: Our team is on the ground in Târgu Mureș and ready to answer anything specific to your property. Schedule a free call or message us on WhatsApp — we respond quickly.

blog_remote.hero_h1: What Remote Owners Need to Know About Renting Property in Romania in 2026
blog_remote.intro: Owning a property in Romania while living abroad is entirely possible — and increasingly common among diaspora Romanians and international investors. However, managing a rental from thousands of kilometres away comes with real legal, fiscal, and logistical responsibilities. This guide covers everything you need to know: from registering your contract with Romanian tax authorities to handling maintenance emergencies without ever stepping on a plane.
blog_remote.s1_h2: Legal Requirements for Renting Property in Romania
blog_remote.s1_body:
Renting property in Romania requires a valid written lease contract and formal registration with the tax authorities. These are not optional formalities — they are legal prerequisites that protect both the landlord and the tenant.

The Rental Contract (Contract de Închiriere)

A Romanian rental contract must be in writing to be legally enforceable. Verbal agreements are not binding for residential tenancies under the Romanian Civil Code (Codul Civil, Articles 1777–1823). The contract must include:

  • Full identification details of both landlord and tenant
  • A precise description of the property (address, surface area, cadastral number)
  • The monthly rent amount and currency
  • The lease term (fixed-term or open-ended)
  • Security deposit terms
  • Responsibilities for maintenance and utilities

Contracts can be signed electronically, which is particularly convenient for remote owners. A digital signature holds full legal validity in Romania under Law No. 455/2001 on electronic signatures.

ANAF Registration

Every rental contract in Romania must be registered with ANAF (Agenția Națională de Administrare Fiscală) within 30 days of signing. This is mandatory regardless of whether the landlord is a Romanian citizen or a foreign national. Failure to register exposes the landlord to administrative fines and prevents the contract from being used as evidence in court.

Registration is done through the ANAF online portal (using a qualified digital certificate) or in person at the local tax office. A property management company can handle registration directly on behalf of a remote owner.

Energy Performance Certificate

Before advertising a property for rent, Romanian law requires a valid energy performance certificate (certificat de performanță energetică). This certificate classifies the property on a scale from A to G. Without it, the property cannot be legally listed or rented.

Key Legal Checklist
  • ✓ Written lease contract in Romanian (or bilingual)
  • ✓ ANAF registration within 30 days of signing
  • ✓ Valid energy performance certificate
  • ✓ Annual income declaration filed with ANAF
blog_remote.s2_h2: Tax Obligations for Landlords in Romania
blog_remote.s2_body:
Rental income in Romania is subject to a flat 10% income tax. Understanding the calculation method and filing requirements is essential before you start collecting rent.

How Romanian Rental Tax Is Calculated

ANAF allows two methods for calculating taxable rental income:

  1. Standard deduction method: ANAF applies an automatic 40% expense deduction. Tax is calculated as 10% of the remaining 60% of gross annual rental income. This is the default option and requires no documentation of actual expenses.
  2. Actual expenses method: Landlords who spend more than 40% of rental income on documented expenses (repairs, maintenance, insurance, depreciation) can declare those instead. This requires careful bookkeeping and receipts.

As a practical example: if your property rents for €400/month (approximately RON 2,000), your gross annual income is approximately RON 24,000. With the standard deduction, taxable income is RON 14,400, and your annual tax bill is RON 1,440 — roughly €290.

Non-Resident Landlords

If you are a Romanian citizen living abroad or a foreign national, you are still obligated to declare and pay Romanian income tax on rental income earned from property located in Romania. Romania has double taxation avoidance treaties with most EU countries, which means you typically will not pay tax twice on the same income — but you must still file in Romania. Consult a Romanian tax advisor or your property management company to understand your specific situation.

Building Association Fees

Most apartments in Romania are part of a asociație de proprietari (building owners' association), which charges monthly fees for common area maintenance, building insurance, elevator maintenance, and other shared expenses. These fees are the landlord's responsibility, though they may be partially recovered from the tenant if stated in the lease.
blog_remote.s3_h2: How Rent Collection Works in Romania
blog_remote.s3_body:
Rent collection in Romania is most reliably done by monthly bank transfer. Cash payments, while legally permitted, are harder to document and create administrative complications for tax purposes.

Security Deposits

Romanian law does not prescribe a specific maximum security deposit amount, but market practice is 1–2 months' rent. The deposit is held by the landlord (or management company) for the duration of the tenancy and returned within a reasonable time after the tenant vacates, minus any legitimate deductions for unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear.

Currency: EUR vs RON

In Târgu Mureș and other Transylvanian cities, rents for higher-quality apartments are commonly quoted in euros, even though Romania's official currency is the Romanian Leu (RON). This protects landlords against local currency fluctuations. The contract should specify whether rent is paid in EUR or RON, and at what exchange rate if conversion is involved.

When Tenants Are Late

A well-drafted lease contract includes penalty clauses for late payment. A professional property management company monitors payment deadlines every month and contacts the tenant immediately if the transfer has not arrived. Most payment issues are resolved within a few days through proactive communication, without escalating to formal legal procedures.
blog_remote.s4_h2: Tenant Rights in Romania You Must Understand
blog_remote.s4_body:
• No eviction without a court order. A landlord cannot force a tenant to leave without going through the courts, regardless of the reason. Even if the tenant has not paid rent, the eviction process requires a judicial procedure that can take several months.
  • Minimum notice periods. For open-ended contracts, the landlord must give at least 30 days' written notice to terminate. Some courts have interpreted the Civil Code as requiring longer periods. The contract should specify the notice period explicitly.
  • Right to use the property undisturbed. A landlord cannot enter the property without the tenant's permission except in a genuine emergency. Regular inspections must be pre-agreed in the lease contract.
  • Rent freeze during fixed-term contracts. A landlord cannot unilaterally raise the rent during a fixed-term lease. Rent increases can only be applied at the start of a new term.

These protections make careful tenant selection before signing the lease the single most important risk management tool available to a landlord.
blog_remote.s5_h2: How to Handle Maintenance from Abroad
blog_remote.s5_body:
Property maintenance is the biggest practical challenge for remote owners. Romanian law assigns clear responsibilities: the landlord is responsible for structural repairs and major systems (heating, plumbing, electrical), while the tenant is responsible for minor day-to-day upkeep.

Landlord vs Tenant Responsibilities

Under the Romanian Civil Code, the landlord must keep the property in a habitable condition throughout the tenancy. This includes repairing major defects that appear during the tenancy (a broken boiler, a leaking roof, a failed lift in a block). The tenant is responsible for minor repairs such as replacing light bulbs, clearing drains of blockages caused by their own use, and general cleaning.

Building a Contractor Network Remotely

Without a local presence, finding reliable contractors at short notice is nearly impossible. A property management company maintains pre-vetted relationships with plumbers, electricians, locksmiths, and general tradespeople. When something breaks, the manager coordinates the repair without requiring any input from the owner — except approval for expenditures above an agreed threshold.

Emergency Response

True property emergencies — burst pipes, heating failure in winter, power outages — cannot wait for a remote owner to research solutions. A professional management company with 24/7 emergency coverage resolves these situations immediately, limiting damage and keeping tenants safe. This is one of the clearest arguments for professional management for any remote owner.
blog_remote.s6_h2: Why Professional Property Management Is the Safest Approach
blog_remote.s6_body:
Self-managing a rental property from abroad is theoretically possible, but in practice it introduces risks that professional management eliminates at a cost that most owners find fully justified.

The Real Costs of Going It Alone

Remote self-management requires navigating Romanian-language bureaucracy (ANAF filings, contract templates, building association correspondence), sourcing and vetting contractors from a distance, handling tenant disputes without local knowledge of legal norms, and being available to respond to emergencies in a different time zone. A single poorly selected tenant or an unresolved maintenance issue can cost far more than a year's management fees.

What a Property Manager Does

A full-service property management company like Velox Living handles the complete lifecycle of your rental: marketing and photography, tenant screening and reference checks, lease drafting, ANAF registration, monthly rent collection with payment monitoring, utility bill management, maintenance coordination, building association payments, periodic property inspections with photo reports, and owner communication in your preferred language.

What This Costs — and What It's Worth

Property management fees in Romania typically range from 8% to 15% of monthly rent, depending on the scope of service. On a €400/month apartment, this amounts to €32–60 per month. Against the risk of a non-paying tenant, an unregistered contract fine, or a maintenance emergency that spirals out of control, this cost is modest. It is also partially offset by lower vacancy rates — professional marketing and rigorous screening reduces the time your property sits empty between tenancies.

Velox Living — Based in Târgu Mureș

Velox Living is a family-run property management company based in Târgu Mureș, Transylvania, serving remote owners and international investors. We operate in English, Romanian, Hungarian and Spanish — with no in-person visit required to get started. View our pricing or contact us on WhatsApp.

blog_remote.faq1_q: Do I need to register my rental contract with ANAF in Romania?
blog_remote.faq1_a: Yes. In Romania, all rental contracts must be registered with ANAF within 30 days of signing. Failure to register can result in fines and makes the contract legally unenforceable in court. The registration can be done online through the ANAF portal or in person at the nearest tax office. A property management company like Velox Living handles this step on behalf of remote owners.
blog_remote.faq2_q: How much income tax do landlords pay in Romania?
blog_remote.faq2_a: Landlords in Romania pay a flat 10% income tax on net rental income. By default, ANAF allows a 40% standard expense deduction, meaning tax is calculated on 60% of gross rental income. Alternatively, landlords can declare actual documented expenses. Non-resident landlords must also register with ANAF and file an annual income declaration.
blog_remote.faq3_q: How does rent collection work in Romania for remote landlords?
blog_remote.faq3_a: Rent in Romania is most commonly collected by monthly bank transfer. A property management company monitors payments each month and follows up immediately if a transfer is late. Security deposits (typically 1–2 months' rent) are held by the landlord or management company and returned to the tenant at the end of the tenancy, minus any legitimate deductions.
blog_remote.faq4_q: What rights do tenants have in Romania that landlords should know about?
blog_remote.faq4_a: Under the Romanian Civil Code, tenants cannot be evicted without a court order, are entitled to at least 30 days' written notice before a landlord-initiated termination, and have the right to use the property undisturbed. Landlords cannot unilaterally raise rent during a fixed-term contract. These protections make thorough tenant screening before signing the lease critical.
blog_remote.faq5_q: Can a landlord living abroad manage a rental in Romania without visiting?
blog_remote.faq5_a: Yes — a landlord living abroad can fully manage a Romanian rental property remotely by appointing a licensed property management company. The management company signs a management mandate, which allows them to conclude lease agreements, register contracts with ANAF, collect rent, coordinate maintenance, and handle all local administration on the owner's behalf. No in-person visits to Romania are required.
blog_remote.faq6_q: What happens if a tenant stops paying rent in Romania?
blog_remote.faq6_a: If a tenant stops paying rent, the landlord must first issue a formal written notice. If unresolved, the landlord can initiate eviction proceedings in court. Romanian civil courts handle eviction cases, but the process can take several months. This is why thorough tenant screening is essential. Professional property managers typically resolve most payment issues through proactive communication before they escalate to legal action.
blog_remote.faq7_q: Is professional property management worth it for remote owners in Romania?
blog_remote.faq7_a: Professional property management is strongly advisable for remote owners in Romania. A qualified property manager handles tenant screening, ANAF registration, rent collection, maintenance coordination, utility bill payments, and compliance with Romanian law. The management fee (typically 8%–15% of monthly rent) is offset by reduced vacancy, fewer legal risks, and the time saved by not dealing with tenant calls and local bureaucracy from abroad.

blog_remote.cta_p: We handle every step — from tenant screening and ANAF registration to rent collection and emergency maintenance — so you can own Romanian property with confidence, from anywhere in the world.

blog_tgm.hero_h1: Property Management in Târgu Mureș: A Complete Guide for Investors
blog_tgm.intro: Târgu Mureș is emerging as one of Romania's most interesting secondary investment markets for residential property. Lower acquisition costs than Bucharest or Cluj-Napoca, a stable long-term tenant base, and improving infrastructure make it worth a serious look. This guide covers the local market, realistic rental yields, the division of responsibilities between property manager and owner, how Transylvania's rental market differs from Bucharest, and the exact steps for working with Velox Living.
blog_tgm.s1_h2: Why Târgu Mureș Is an Interesting Investment Market
blog_tgm.s1_body:
Târgu Mureș (Marosvásárhely in Hungarian, Neumarkt am Mieresch in German) is the capital of Mureș County, with a population of approximately 120,000–130,000 people. It is the largest city in Transylvania after Cluj-Napoca and Brașov, and one of the few genuinely bilingual cities in Romania where both Romanian and Hungarian are spoken as everyday languages.

Demand Drivers

The city's rental market is driven by several structural demand factors that provide a stable foundation for buy-to-let investment:

  • George Emil Palade University (UMFST) — one of Romania's leading medical and pharmacy universities, with approximately 10,000 students, a significant portion of whom rent privately. Medical students tend to be reliable, long-term tenants who stay for 6-year programmes.
  • Healthcare sector professionals — Târgu Mureș hosts multiple hospitals and medical research institutions. Medical professionals represent a high-quality tenant demographic with stable income.
  • Industrial employment base — Manufacturing companies including Romgaz (Romania's state gas producer) and numerous international firms in the local industrial zone provide stable working-class demand for affordable rentals.
  • Bilingual appeal — The city's unique Romanian-Hungarian character attracts tenants from both linguistic communities, broadening the effective tenant pool.

Infrastructure and Connectivity

Târgu Mureș has a functioning international airport (TGM) with seasonal and regular connections to major European hubs. The road network connecting it to Cluj-Napoca (approximately 110 km) and Brașov (approximately 150 km) has seen continued investment. For investors, this means the city is accessible for periodic visits and has genuine long-term growth potential rather than isolation risk.

Price Environment in 2026

Average apartment acquisition prices in Târgu Mureș in 2026 range approximately from €800–€1,400 per square metre for existing stock, depending on location, floor, and condition. New-build properties in premium developments reach €1,500–€1,900/m². Central and western residential neighbourhoods (Tudor, Unirii, Cornești) command the highest rents relative to purchase price. These figures represent significant discounts — typically 40%–60% — versus equivalent properties in Bucharest or Cluj-Napoca.
blog_tgm.s2_h2: Average Rental Yields in Târgu Mureș
blog_tgm.s2_body:
Gross rental yields in Târgu Mureș typically range from 5% to 8% per year, depending on the property type, neighbourhood, condition, and the quality of tenants secured. This compares favourably with major Western European markets and is competitive with the larger Romanian cities when accounting for lower acquisition costs.

A Practical Yield Example

A 2-bedroom apartment in good condition in the Tudor neighbourhood, purchased for €80,000 and rented at €420/month, generates gross annual income of €5,040 — a gross yield of 6.3%. After management fees (approximately 10%), building association fees, and the 10% Romanian income tax (applied to 60% of gross income under the standard deduction), net yield is approximately 4.5%–5.2%, depending on vacancy and maintenance costs.

Yield by Property Type

  • Studio / 1-bedroom apartments (garsonieră/apartament 1 cameră): Strong demand from students; yields 6%–8%; lower absolute rent but very low vacancy.
  • 2-bedroom apartments: The most liquid segment; yields 5.5%–7%; suits couples, young professionals, and medical residents.
  • 3-bedroom apartments: Yields 5%–6.5%; attracts families and shared professional tenants; slightly longer void periods between tenancies.
  • Commercial / retail spaces: Yields can exceed 8%; higher risk profile; specialist market knowledge essential.
blog_tgm.s3_h2: How Transylvania's Rental Market Differs from Bucharest
blog_tgm.s3_body:

The key distinction is that Târgu Mureș is a long-term rental market. The student and professional tenant base typically stays for one to several years. This means lower turnover costs, more stable cash flow, and a simpler management operation compared to the more transactional Bucharest market. For investors seeking passive income rather than capital gains speculation, this stability is a significant advantage.
blog_tgm.s4_h2: What a Property Manager Handles vs What the Owner Handles
blog_tgm.s4_body:
A common point of confusion for first-time investors is the exact division of responsibility between the property manager and the owner. The model at Velox Living is straightforward: we handle everything operational; the owner retains control over strategic and capital decisions.

blog_tgm.faq4_q: Can a foreign investor buy and rent out property in Târgu Mureș?
blog_tgm.faq4_a: Yes. EU citizens have had the same property ownership rights as Romanian nationals since 2007. Non-EU nationals can legally own apartments and commercial spaces in Romania without restriction. Renting out your property is fully legal: you register the lease with ANAF, declare rental income annually, and pay a flat 10% income tax. Romania has double taxation treaties with most major countries. A property management company like Velox Living handles all local administration on behalf of foreign owners.

The university academic calendar creates strong seasonal demand in August–September. Properties that are professionally photographed and listed on major Romanian portals consistently rent faster.
